The Curse of Being the Emperor's Firstborn.
Imagine being born as the first son of the most powerful emperor in the world.
People would say you were blessed.
Born into a life of endless wealth, surrounded by gold, servants, and unimaginable luxury. One day, you would inherit the throne and rule an entire empire.
But what they don't know... is that being born into the royal family is not always a blessing.
Sometimes, it's a curse.
The moment I was born, my fate was already decided.
I was not born to live my own life.
I was born to become the next emperor.
Before I could even walk, my future had already been written. Every word I spoke, every action I took, and every decision I made was carefully watched.
My father, the Emperor, never saw me as a child.
He saw me as his successor.

At the age of five, I was forced to study history, politics, and military strategy. While other children played in the gardens, I sat in a cold classroom, memorizing the names of kings and the history of wars.
At seven, I began sword training.
At ten, I was taught how to command soldiers and identify enemies.
And by the age of twelve, I had already learned one terrifying truth:
In the imperial palace, nobody can truly be trusted.
My brothers saw me as an obstacle.
The nobles saw me as a political tool.
And even the people who smiled at me every day might secretly be waiting for my downfall.
There were countless attempts on my life.
Poison hidden in my food. Assassins lurking in the shadows. Accidents that were never really accidents.
I learned to inspect every meal before eating. I learned to sleep with a dagger beneath my pillow. And I learned never to turn my back on anyone.
Imagine that.
Living in a palace filled with treasures, yet never feeling safe enough to close your eyes.
People outside the palace envied me.
They wished they could have my wealth, my title, and my future.
But none of them understood.
I would trade every piece of gold, every palace, and even the throne itself just to experience an ordinary childhood.
To have friends who didn't care about my status.
To laugh without worrying about political consequences.
To sleep peacefully without wondering if tomorrow would be my last day.
But I couldn't.
Because I was the firstborn son of the Emperor.
And in this empire, the crown was not a reward.
It was a sentence.
A sentence I had been forced to carry since the day I was born.
